- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.7) and forecast is rising sharply, reduce overshoot by 5–10% to avoid overcorrection.  
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.3) and forecast is falling, avoid premature bottoming — maintain slight upward bias to capture mean reversion.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >5%), reduce next-period forecast by 3–5% to account for momentum decay.  
- If sentiment is neutral (0.3–0.67) and forecast deviates >3% from true, apply mean reversion correction toward recent 7-day average.  
- For 30-day horizon, if forecast is consistently > true by 2–4% over 3–5 days, adjust downward by 1–2% per day to reflect diminishing momentum.  
- When sentiment is mixed (0.0–0.3) and forecast is erratic, anchor to 14-day moving average to reduce noise-driven overfitting.
